For claim c1:

Mayo Clinic states that assertions about COVID-19 vaccines containing microchips for tracking or gathering personal information are false. [1] [2] This myth originated from comments made by Bill Gates about a digital certificate of vaccine records, but the technology he referenced is not a microchip and is not tied to COVID-19 vaccine development or distribution. [1] FactCheck.org also debunks a similar claim, explaining that a chip discussed by a medical device company executive was for tracking vaccine doses, not people, and would be attached to the vial, not injected. [3] Indonesian government sources, such as the Ministry of Communication and Information and the COVID-19 Handling Task Force, have also stated that the claim of microchips in vaccines for tracking people is false. [4] [5] [6] They clarify that barcodes on vaccine products are for tracking distribution and do not get implanted into individuals. [4] [5] Experts and medical professionals consistently affirm that it is impossible to put tracking microchips in COVID-19 vaccines due to size and technological limitations. [7]
